newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CHARGES FRAMED AGAINST FORMER PREMIER

Charges of criminal conspiracy and cheating were framed against former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and co-accused Chandraswamy and Kailash Nath Aggarwal in the Lakhubhai Pathak cheating case. All the accused pleaded not guilty and challenged to contest the trial. Narasimha Rao was, however, granted bail in the case. He was granted bail on the furnishing of a personal bond of 100,000 rupees and a surety of the same amount.
The Economic Times
KAWASAKI STEEL BUYING STAKE IN MUKAND

Japanese major Kawasaki Steel Corporation is likely to pick up a 20 percent equity stake in Mukand Vijayanagar Steel Ltd. The exact equity holding by the Japanese company is being worked out on the basis of debt-equity ratio. Kawasaki Steel will supply the blast furnace technology for the five million metric tonne hot rolled coils project of Mukand. Total investment in the three-stage five million metric tonne capacity plant is expected to be around 120 billion rupees.
SENSEX BOUNCES BACK AFTER BREACHING 3,000 MARK

The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) sensitive index broke the psychological barrier of 3000-mark and touched an intra-day low of 2999.79. However, hectic short-covering before the closure of trading session pushed up the index to 3044.16, a net loss of 16.09 points over the previous closing. The sharp fall in mid-session was largely led by the crash in the ITC counter amid allegations against it for violation of foreign exchange rules involving over $100 million.
BAT WANTS COMPLETE OVERHAUL OF ITC BOARD

BAT Industries Plc has asked financial institutions (FIs) to consider the removal of all executive directors on the ITC board, including chairman Yogi Deveshwar. The suggestion has been made by BAT in a bid to clean the battered image of the tobacco giant. According to sources FIs would prefer to wait and watch for some more days before arriving at a decision. The FIs have decided to announce their blueprint for the new corporate structure at the November 15 board meeting of the ITC Ltd.
BRAKES ON LIQUID FUEL-BASED POWER PROJECTS

The power ministry has asked the State governments not to commit themselves to any new liquid fuel based power projects. The ministry is re-evaluating its policy on liquid fuel-based power projects in view of a likely short fall in crude oil production. Under present shortages, naphtha-based power projects could not be encouraged, ministry sources said. The ministry is reportedly re-evaluating its liquid fuel policy which was announced to promote projects based on alternative fuel.
Financial Express
NO EXIT POLICY AT WORKERS' COST

Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said the government would announce a promotional package for the small scale sector soon but ruled out an exit policy. The government could not have an exit policy at the cost of workers and it needed to go slow on the matter, Maran said. The minister said Voluntary Retirement Scheme was being made more attractive to minimise social distress.
Business Standard
ISPAT INDIA PLAN TO FLOAT BASIC SERVICES HOLDING COMPANY

Ispat India has sought the Department of Telecommunications' permission to float a holding company. This is the first ever holding company to be proposed in basic telecommunication services. Ispat India holds 51 percent stake in Hughes Ispat. The latter has provisional licences for basic services in Maharashtra. The proposed holding company, christened Ispat Telecom Holding Pvt Ltd, will have a 48 percent foreign equity stake. The equity of the holding company will be used to finance Ispat's 51 percent stake in Hughes Ispat.
RESTRUCTURING PACKAGE FOR 49 STATE FIRMS FINALISED

The industry ministry has finalised a restructuring package for the 49 public sector units (PSUs) in the heavy industry sector. The package includes provisions for greater autonomy to PSU managements and reduction of the workforce. Outlining the plan, the industry minister said the PSUs would be placed in four categories. Top 10 profit making PSUs (excluding PSU giant Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd) will be developed into global players through the joint venture route.
OIL POOL DEFICIT LIKELY TO INCREASE

The oil pool deficit at the end of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) would touch 155 billion rupees as against the initial projection of 97 billion rupees, the junior petroleum minister revealed. The minister's statement has given rise to fears of another hike in the petroleum goods price. The current oil pool deficit is estimated at 80 billion rupees. The minister attributed the higher deficit to the four percent depreciation in the value of the rupee, increase in imports, rise in international prices, dip in domestic crude production and non-adjustment of selling prices. The oil import bill in the first half of 1996/97 rose 40 percent to $4.4 billion.
The Observer
PLAN PANEL FOR CAP ON REVENUE DEFICIT

The Planning Commission favours a ceiling on government for bringing about fiscal consolidation. Madhu Dandavate, the Planning Commission deputy chairman, called for a consensus on installing a system of capping government's borrowing. He said the Planning Commission would soon make a formal proposal in this regard. The commission's proposal envisaged a cap on revenue deficit.
